title: The Strike Committee
speaker: interior
body: {speaker} reports that the mills of {town} have fallen silent. A strike committee demands shorter hours and a living wage, and the garrison asks for orders.

options.label: Meet their demands
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.3 months of GDP · grievance −20 · a concession the world will notice

options.label: Send in the militia
options.tooltip: Grievance −10 now, but a crackdown is remembered at home and abroad

options.label: Wait it out
options.tooltip: Nothing is spent; nothing is settled

effects.log: The strike drags on in {town}; the committee paints its demands on the town hall.

title: The Martyrs of the Mill
speaker: people
body: A year on, crowds gather in {town} to lay flowers where the strikers fell. The organisers have a name for the day now, and a list of demands longer than before.

options.label: Permit the memorial
options.tooltip: Grievance −8 · legitimacy +3

options.label: Ban the gathering
options.tooltip: A second crackdown — the movement goes underground

title: Shots at the Frontier Post
speaker: rival
body: {speaker} accuses our border guards of firing on a customs patrol. {rivalLeader} demands an apology and indemnity — or 'consequences'.

options.label: Apologise and pay
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.2 months of GDP · relations with them +12

options.label: Demand our own inquiry
options.tooltip: Relations −4 · nothing conceded

effects.log: Our inquiry into the frontier shooting convenes; {rival} calls it a whitewash.

options.label: Mobilise the border garrisons
options.tooltip: War support +10 · relations −15 · an act of aggression

title: Troops on Both Banks
speaker: defence
body: {speaker} reports that {rival} has answered our mobilisation in kind. Two armies now eye each other across the river. One false step and the century decides for us.

options.label: Stand down, quietly
options.tooltip: War support −8 · relations +10

options.label: Hold the line
options.tooltip: Relations −5 · the standoff hardens

title: Bankers from Abroad
speaker: treasury
body: {speaker} brings word that financiers backed by {friend} will extend credit — in exchange for favourable access to our markets.

options.label: Take the money
options.tooltip: Treasury +1 month of GDP · confidence −5 · relations with them +6

options.label: Decline politely
options.tooltip: Confidence +3

title: The Ledger Affair
speaker: press
body: {speaker} warns that a newspaper holds copies of ministry ledgers showing contracts steered to friends of the government. It goes to print on Friday.

options.label: Let it run and sack the ministers
options.tooltip: Legitimacy −4 now, +political capital later · free press

options.label: Seize the presses
options.tooltip: Scandal buried · censorship remembered

title: Refugees at the Gates
speaker: interior
body: Families fleeing {rival} gather at our border posts. {speaker} asks whether we open the gates — {rivalLeader} will call it interference either way.

options.label: Open the gates
options.tooltip: Humane deed · relations with them −6 · a small strain at home

options.label: Close the border
options.tooltip: No strain · relations +3

title: The Neighbours Arm
speaker: foreign
body: {speaker} warns that our record has frightened the chanceries. Several powers are quietly comparing notes on us.

options.label: Launch a peace initiative
options.tooltip: Political capital −2 · relations +4 with everyone

options.label: Let them fear us
options.tooltip: War support +5 · relations −3 with everyone

title: Our Word Is Worthless
speaker: foreign
body: {speaker} reports that envoys now demand hostages, bonds and third-party guarantees before they will sign anything with us.

options.label: Post a good-faith bond
options.tooltip: Treasury −0.25 months of GDP · relations +5 with everyone

options.label: Ignore the whispering
options.tooltip: Nothing changes
